statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let B be the set of all integers i such that Occ(s,a,i) and there exists an integer j with Occ(s,b,j) and |j - i| <= k. Then r, viewed as a sequence of mathematical integers, is exactly the elements of B in strictly increasing order: len(r) = |B|, and for every t with 0 <= t < len(r), r[t] is the unique element of B having exactly t elements of B smaller than it. Here Occ(x,t,p) means 0 <= p, p + len(t) <= len(x), and for every q with 0 <= q < len(t), x[p+q] = t[q].
preconditions: Let len(x) be the byte length of slice x and x[p] its p-th byte. s, a, and b contain only lowercase ASCII letters. 1 <= len(s) <= 500000, 1 <= len(a) <= 500000, 1 <= len(b) <= 500000, and k is an i64 representing a mathematical integer with 1 <= k <= len(s). No assumption is made that len(a) <= len(s) or len(b) <= len(s).
